name: Electric toothbrushes and shavers

comps.spec: One 3.6–3.7V lithium-ion cell, about AA size (14 by 49 mm on the Oral-B iO and Sonicare HX6710, 14500 size on the Philips S5000 shaver) in newer models
One or two 1.2V NiMH cells in older and budget models
Small 1.2–3.7V DC motor (shavers, clippers, rotating brushes)
Neodymium magnets in the resonant drive (sonic toothbrushes)
Inductive charging stand with a coil (toothbrushes) or a small adapter
Coil that picks up power from the charging stand, soldered to the main board (the iO's charging coil sits at the bottom end; the Sonicare Flexcare Platinum charges at about 80 kHz)
Small board in the handle: the motor, charging coil and cell are soldered to it; the Bluetooth Oral-B iO's also carries a Bluetooth chip, a Hall sensor and an OLED screen
Hall effect sensor on the Oral-B iO's board that reads a small magnet on a flexible plastic piece to sense brushing pressure (not found in the other logged brushes)
Frictionless coil motor in the Oral-B iO: a coil that gives straight up-and-down brush motion with no cam or gear, held by Torx 8 screws

notes: Handles are sealed and often closed tight round the cell. Open one only the way it was made to open (a twist-off cap or screws), use plastic tools in any seam, and never put a blade or screwdriver in a seam: you could puncture the cell.

sources.title: Open Repair Alliance, Open Repair Data v0.3 (community repair events, 2012 to July 2026; CC BY-SA 4.0): 949 repairs recorded as Hair & beauty item (electric toothbrush subset)
